material_rulings.evidence: Lev.23.23-25 and 23.26-32 are separately framed speeches with different dates, observances, requirements, and sanctions. The second unit also directly corresponds to the annual observance in Lev.16.29-34. Adjacency within the seventh month does not overcome the functional change.

replacements.title: Day of Atonement observance, sanctions, and Sabbath bounds

revision_operation.coverage_preservation: The ordered union exactly equals Lev.23.23-Lev.23.32 without gap or overlap.

material_rulings.dissent_preserved: The two observances are adjacent seventh-month convocations, and the strategy cautions that a speech reset alone is insufficient.

material_rulings.evidence: Lev.26.1-2 supplies an allegiance frame and Lev.26.3 begins the explicit conditional blessing. No new speech begins at Lev.26.1, while splitting at 26.3 would create a detached two-verse frame. The larger unit remains plausible but must stay related to the uninterrupted Lev.25.1-26.46 Sinai discourse.
material_rulings.dissent_preserved: Conditional syntax at Lev.26.3 strongly supports an alternative blessing boundary; Lev.26.1-2 may also bridge directly from Lev.25.

material_rulings.evidence: Lev.23.1-3 presents the overarching appointed-time heading and weekly Sabbath. Lev.23.4 repeats the heading and begins the dated annual calendar with Passover and Unleavened Bread. The repeated frame coincides with a genuine weekly-to-annual calendrical function change.

replacements.title: Annual appointed-times heading, Passover, and Unleavened Bread

revision_operation.coverage_preservation: The ordered union exactly equals Lev.23.1-Lev.23.8 without gap or overlap.

material_rulings.dissent_preserved: The weekly Sabbath belongs to the overarching appointed-time framework, favoring one larger calendar opening.

material_rulings.evidence: Lev.18.24-30 is explicitly backward-dependent on the preceding acts and completes the speech through land-defilement, expulsion, cut-off, and guarding language. Nevertheless, its rationale-and-sanction function differs from the prohibition series in 18.1-23, supporting retrieval children beneath an inseparable Lev.18.1-30 parent.
material_rulings.dissent_preserved: The grammatical and rhetorical dependence of 18.24-30 supplies substantial evidence for physically merging the two decisions.

material_rulings.evidence: Lev.17.10-14 governs blood consumption and hunted-game draining; 17.15-16 shifts to carrion-related washing and temporary impurity, corresponding in form to Lev.11.39-40. The shift is real, but a two-verse standalone child would over-fragment one resident-inclusive consumption speech.

revision_operation.title: Blood consumption, hunted game, and carcass handling

material_rulings.dissent_preserved: The paragraph and procedural shift at Lev.17.15 could justify a distinct carrion-cleansing unit.
